beats.text: Your ADHD brain isn't bad with money. It's bad at remembering.
beats.why: Reassure-and-reframe hook. Pattern from @yourmoneymatesarah ('You're not inherently bad with money…', 403.5k views, 4.7% saves) + @adhd_chatter_podcast ('Stop trusting your memory', 383.8k views, 6.4% saves). Text on screen from frame 1.

beats.text: Payday hits, and five minutes later you've found three new hobbies.
beats.why: Relatable payday-dopamine joke. Pattern from @inflow (407.4k views, 10.7k shares): humor drives shares.

beats.text: So stop making your brain remember. Make your bank do it.
beats.why: Re-hook at about 8s: promise of a solution, so viewers who related now stay.
Numbered-list promise. Pattern from @priceofavocadotoast ('three types of bank accounts every human with ADHD needs', 154.6k views, 6.9% saves, the highest save rate in the sample).

beats.text: Bills. Autopay pulls from it. You never even look at it.
beats.why: List payoff, one beat per item.

beats.text: Spend. Your card, and the only balance you ever check.
Buffer. Oops money, so one surprise doesn't wreck everything.
Goals. Money with a name on it is way harder to impulse spend.
beats.why: List payoff + impulse-spend pain (adhd impulse spending is a documented sub-topic).

beats.text: And the best part? It keeps working on the weeks you forget it exists.
beats.why: Intensifier: removes the biggest objection (I always fall off). Mirrors the product promise.

beats.text: Save this for payday. The full setup is called Forget-Proof Money. It's in my bio.
beats.why: Save prompt (saves are the intent signal we optimise for) + soft product CTA with the exact product name.
